entries.doc: The routine decides. Consume: `moveq #1,%d0; rts` (the event reaches no view and no release callback; the runner's idle reset and the Brain+0x94 listeners already ran). Pass: the displaced `lea; movem` and a jump to the end of the site (the tail). Strict liveness at the tail: only the flags (N, Z, V, C) are dead; D0, D1, A0 and A1 are live (the stock code calls a function that may read them), so a routine saves them; D2 and A2 are saved by the displaced `movem` itself.
entries.name: cf.input.hook.key_event

entries.doc: The second reader of the LFO tables, the compare of D3 with 6 before the call of the wave function table (interrupt context; d7 is live). exit.1 is the RAND code, exit.2 the code after the call. DT2 0x401394dc: `moveq 6,D0; cmp.l D3,D0; beq 0x40139512`. Dead at the RAND code (0x40139512): D0 and the flags; at the code after the call (0x4013957a): D2, D3, A6 and the flags, D1 and D0 are live. The stock fall-through needs the upper bits of D0 clear (`move.b #0x32,D0b` after the moveq): the routine sets D0 itself. The block is A4 (wave byte at 0x2a(a4)).
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_call

entries.doc: The second reader of the LFO tables, the compare of D3 with 6 before the call of the wave function table (interrupt context; d7 is live). exit.1 is the RAND code, exit.2 the code after the call. DN2 0x401378c4: `moveq 6,D0; cmp.l D3,D0; beq 0x401378fa`. Dead at the RAND code (0x401378fa): D0 and the flags; at the code after the call (0x40137962): D2, D3, A6 and the flags, D1 and D0 are live. The stock fall-through needs the upper bits of D0 clear (`move.b #0x32,D0b` after the moveq): the routine sets D0 itself. The block is A4 (wave byte at 0x2a(a4)).
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_call

entries.doc: The second reader, the compare of D3 with 6 before the slew code (interrupt context). exit.1 skips the slew code. DT2 0x4013954a: `moveq 6,D2; cmp.l D3,D2; bne 0x4013957a`. Dead where the stock fall-through (0x40139550) continues: D0, D2, D3, A1, A6 and N Z V C; at 0x4013957a: D2, D3, A6 and the flags.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_slew

entries.doc: The second reader, the compare of D3 with 6 before the slew code (interrupt context). exit.1 skips the slew code. DN2 0x40137932: `moveq 6,D2; cmp.l D3,D2; bne 0x40137962`. Dead where the stock fall-through (0x40137938) continues: D0, D2, D3, A1, A6 and N Z V C; at 0x40137962: D2, D3, A6 and the flags.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_slew

entries.doc: The second reader, the compare of D3 with 6 that gives RAND a start phase of 0 (interrupt context). exit.1 is the clear. DT2 0x4013944e: `moveq 6,D2; cmp.l D3,D2; beq 0x4013946a`. Dead at the clear (0x4013946a): D2, D6 and N Z V C; at the SPH phase code (0x40139454): D0, D2, D6 and N Z V C.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_start

entries.doc: The second reader, the compare of D3 with 6 that gives RAND a start phase of 0 (interrupt context). exit.1 is the clear. DN2 0x40137836: `moveq 6,D2; cmp.l D3,D2; beq 0x40137852`. Dead at the clear (0x40137852): D2, D6 and N Z V C; at the SPH phase code (0x4013783c): D0, D2, D6 and N Z V C.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.read_start

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of the clamped wave D3 with 6 before the call of the wave function table (interrupt context). exit.1 is the RAND code, exit.2 the code after the call (the result in d0); the end of the site is the table call of the stock waves. DT2 0x40139804: `moveq 6,D7; cmp.l D3,D7; beq 0x40139832`. Dead at the RAND code (0x40139832): D0 and the flags (strict); at the code after the call (0x4013989e): D2, D3, D5, D7 and the flags, D1 is live (the stock call path keeps it in its frame, the routine saves it); A0 and A1 are not proven dead there (strict), so the routine saves them too. The block is A3 (wave byte at 2(a3)).
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_call

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of the clamped wave D3 with 6 before the call of the wave function table (interrupt context). exit.1 is the RAND code, exit.2 the code after the call (the result in d0); the end of the site is the table call of the stock waves. DN2 0x40137cc6: `moveq 6,D0; cmp.l D3,D0; beq 0x40137cec`. Dead at the RAND code (0x40137cec): D0 and the flags; at the code after the call (0x40137d52): D1, D2 and the flags (the DN2 stock call path keeps no register in its frame, so the routine saves no D1); A0 and A1 are not proven dead there (strict), so the routine saves them. The block is A4 (wave byte at 0x4c(a4)).
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_call

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of D3 with 6 before the slew code of RAND (interrupt context). exit.1 skips the slew code; the end of the site is the slew code. DT2 0x4013986c: `moveq 6,D2; cmp.l D3,D2; bne 0x4013989e`. Dead where the stock fall-through (the slew code, 0x40139872) continues: D0, D2, D3, D5, D7, A0, A1 and N Z V C; at 0x4013989e: D2, D3, D5, D7 and the flags. D0 (the table result) and D1 are live.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_slew

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of D3 with 6 before the slew code of RAND (interrupt context). exit.1 skips the slew code; the end of the site is the slew code. Dead where the stock fall-through (the slew code, 0x40137d24) continues: D0, D1, D2, A0, A1 and N Z V C; at 0x40137d52: D1, D2 and the flags. D0 (the table result) is live.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_slew

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of D3 with 6 that gives RAND a start phase of 0 at a trigger (interrupt context). exit.1 is the clear; the end of the site is the SPH-based phase. DT2 0x4013977e: `moveq 6,D0; cmp.l D3,D0; beq 0x4013979a`. Dead at the clear (0x4013979a): D1, D2, D7 and N Z V C; at the SPH phase code (0x40139784): D0, D1, D2, D7 and N Z V C.
entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_start

entries.doc: The LFO tick, the compare of D3 with 6 that gives RAND a start phase of 0 at a trigger (interrupt context). exit.1 is the clear; the end of the site is the SPH-based phase. entries.name: cf.lfo.hook.tick_start

entries.doc: Sets the title-bar flag at +0x1b8 of a CompactVerticalMenuView. entries.doc: `MmcFs *f(void)`: the card file system singleton (the getter of `std::_Sp_counted_ptr<MmcFs*>`; DT2 1.17 0x4019dbda, DN2 1.12 0x4018e0a8, DN2 1.11 0x4018ddc8; the code differs per image, the hash is unique on each). The firmware's listing of the 129 slots is in it [V]: the record of slot s is at +0x10 + s * 0x1c (slot 0x80 is the live mirror): byte 0 is nonzero when the slot exists (the name, header byte 8, is not empty; the firmware's own accessors test only this byte), byte 1 is 1 for a `DT1P` or `DN1P` header and 0 for the in-memory format magic 0xBEEFBACE, the u32 at +4 is a record format word [D] (5 on a cleared project), the 16 name bytes at +8 (no terminator is written), the u32 at +0x18 is the save stamp (header +0x18). The listing refresh `(MmcFs *, slot)` (DT2 0x4012f2fa, DN2 0x4012dbce) fills it and takes a mutex at +0x1e030 (DN2) or +0x1e034 (DT2) at entry. A header that cannot be read leaves the name "ERROR" with bytes 0 and 1 zero [D], unless the static header buffer still holds a valid magic. The project service reads name and stamp there. Not found on Syntakt.
entries.name: cf.project.fn.mmcfs

entries.name: cf.project.hook.clear_many_exit

entries.doc: At the exit of the clear callback, after the card write and the listing refresh: records the slot **(0x3c(SP)) as cleared, always (a failed clear then archives a `.dkp` that is still needed, which is recoverable). The routine saves D0, D1, D2, A0, A1 and the flags (strict liveness proves only A0 dead).
entries.name: cf.project.hook.clear_one_exit

entries.doc: Before the rts of the paste: when D0.b is nonzero it records the destination slot D6 as pasted over (a paste that did not reach the card write records nothing). The routine saves D1, A0, A1 and the flags and keeps D0 and D6.
entries.name: cf.project.hook.paste_exit

entries.doc: Before the rts of the save: when D0.b is nonzero and D3 is not 0x80 it records the slot D3. Strict liveness leaves every register and the flags live at the return, so the routine saves D1 and the flags and keeps D0 and D3.
entries.name: cf.project.hook.save_exit

entries.doc: Records the slot the setter was called with (also a call with the current slot: the setter ignores it, so the service does) and runs the displaced `mvs.b` in the tail. D1 and the flags are written by that instruction first.
entries.name: cf.project.hook.slot_set

entries.doc: DT2 0x400a13e6, DN2 1.12 0x4009b55c (function DT2 0x400a1376, DN2 0x4009b4ec, + 0x70): the exit of the job callback of the stock clear of several projects (`bool f(Job **)`, run on the BgWorker thread, finishes its writes and refresh inside the job: **arg is a vector of 32-bit slots, begin at +0 and end at +4): `movem.l (SP),D2-D5/A2-A6; lea 0x34(SP),SP` (8 bytes, a plain copy); the rts follows. The job is at 0x38(SP); D0.b is the AND of the per-slot results. Checked against image bytes [V].
entries.name: cf.project.site.clear_many_exit

entries.doc: DT2 0x400a1368, DN2 1.12 0x4009b4de (function DT2 0x400a131e, DN2 0x4009b494, + 0x4a): the exit of the job callback of the stock clear of one project (`bool f(Job **)`, run on the BgWorker thread: slot = **arg, then the slot record is reset, written to the card and the listing refreshed, all inside the job): `movem.l 0x1c(SP),D2/A2/A3` (6 bytes, a plain copy); `lea 0x38(SP),SP; moveq 1,D0; rts` follow. SP is the entry SP - 0x38, so the job is at 0x3c(SP); D2 still holds the slot. The function always returns 1. Checked against image bytes [V].
entries.name: cf.project.site.clear_one_exit

entries.doc: DT2 0x400f55aa, DN2 1.12 0x400f6f86, DN2 1.11 0x400f6dba (function DT2 0x400f548e, DN2 0x400f6e6a, DN2 1.11 0x400f6c9e, + 0x11c): the one exit of the stock project paste `bool paste(ProjectCache *, int slot, bool)` (it runs on the BgWorker thread: it copies the clipboard's project over the slot record, stamp and name included, writes the card and refreshes the listing, all inside the job): `movem.l -0x38(A6),D2-D6/A2; unlk A6` (8 bytes, a plain copy; the rts follows). D0.b is nonzero when the copy reached the card write (the write's own result, `FUN_400f5150`, is discarded and not returned), D6 and 12(A6) the destination slot, A6 the frame. The function is found as the target of the `jsr` at +0x16 of the paste job callback (DT2 0x400a12f8, DN2 0x4009b46e, one strict hash on both), because the function's own strict hash differs between the devices (the project size is an immediate); `offset` is added to that target. Checked against image bytes [V]; bytes equal on all three images.
entries.name: cf.project.site.paste_exit

entries.doc: DT2 0x40043b1e, DN2 0x4004027e: the one exit of the stock project save `int save(Project *, int slot, progress)` (the only rts is the next instruction): `movem.l (SP),D2-D4/A2-A6; lea 0x34(SP),SP` (8 bytes, a plain copy). D0.b is nonzero when the card write succeeded and D3 is the slot (0x80 on the mirror save).
entries.name: cf.project.site.save_exit

entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.reset.init_calls

entries.doc: Semaphore init (0x40001398 on all three images). A semaphore is 8 bytes: +0 count or flag, +4 the one waiting TCB (one waiter only). No static initialiser.
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.sem_init

entries.doc: Binary semaphore pend (0x4000141a on all three images): if the flag is set it clears it and returns, else the task blocks (trap #0). No timeout; task context only.
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.sem_pend

entries.doc: Binary semaphore post (0x4000155c on all three images): masks SR, sets the flag, readies the waiter and forces the reschedule interrupt. ISR-safe (the DTIM1 interrupt posts the sleep semaphore this way). Posts coalesce: the waiter must drain its work after each wake. Shares its hash with cf.rtos.fn.task_start (ordinal 2).
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.sem_post

entries.doc: Stock short sleep (DT2 1.17 0x40136544, DN2 1.12 0x4013492c, DN2 1.11 0x4013464c; DT2 stock name dtim1_sleep_100us): locks its own mutex, loads timer DTIM1 (prescaler 0x84, about 1 MHz) with `us` and blocks the task on a semaphore until the timer interrupt. Task context only. The LP0 sender waits 100 after each page with it; the runtime's I/O task uses it for delays (the kernel has no timed pend).
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.sleep_us

entries.doc: Kernel task init (0x400012c8 on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12 and DN2 1.11; the kernel is byte-identical): fills the caller's TCB (at least 0x54 bytes) for priority `prio` (0 to 15, higher wins; above 15 overwrites the current-TCB pointer) and builds the first RTE frame at the top of the caller's stack (entry gets no argument and must never return). Writes only the TCB and the stack; returns 1. The task runs after cf.rtos.fn.task_start. Stock creates tasks this way from the boot thread and, after the scheduler runs, from the main-OS task (the progress screen).
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.task_create
entries.sig: i32 (u32 tcb, u32 entry, u32 prio, u32 stack, u32 size)

entries.doc: Kernel task start (0x40001314 on all three images): links the TCB into its priority's ready ring under SR 0x2700; does not reschedule. The hash is shared by three identical wrappers (0x40001314, 0x4000132c, 0x4000155c), hence the ordinal.
entries.name: cf.rtos.fn.task_start
